label: Contingent-support rival of the no-contingent-support premise survives, checked
description: Rival test for the no-contingent-support premise against its smallest consumer, NecessaryConcreteUnderived.checks (premises: concrete population, well-founded actual grounding, contingent dependence, reflexive access at the selected world, no contingent concrete support, well-founded union of necessary support, excluded middle). With a necessary whole that is a root at the selected world and is grounded at another world by a part existing only there, the rival holds with the other six premises and no necessary concretum is underived at every admitted world. Model-witnessed survival only.

research_comparisons.conditions: Control.sustainedWhole at world false: the rival, concrete population, ActualGroundingWF, EveryContingentGroundedAt, ActualReflexive, ConcreteNecessaryUnionWF and excluded middle hold; NecessaryConcreteUnderivedAt fails. Consumer tested: NecessaryConcreteUnderived.checks.
research_comparisons.scope: Same Profile, selected relation and selected world as the premise; two mutually accessible worlds, three candidates, all concrete.
research_comparisons.coverage: One explicitly populated interpretation. In it the necessary whole is unsupported at the selected world and supported only elsewhere; the other premises force some necessary actual root, so a rival model with support at the selected world itself needs a second necessary candidate and is not exhibited.
research_comparisons.exclusivity: The rival and the premise cannot both hold on one Profile and world (unregistered helper contingentSupport_excludes).
research_comparisons.witness: Control.sustainedWhole in Control.ContingentSupportSurvives; contingentSupportSurvives proves the listed conjuncts.
research_comparisons.next_step: Decide whether the direction of the selected relation may differ between worlds for the same pair of kinds (whole grounds part here, part grounds whole there); an invariance premise on the relation would exclude this interpretation.
